patch.diff touches only rdflib/extras/shacl.py and test/test_extras/test_extras_shacl.py; pyproject.toml and poetry.lock are untouched.
The module uses only rdflib and stdlib typing, with no new third-party dependency.
The parser is a pure function in the extras layer (rdflib/extras/shacl.py:19-94), the same placement as the reference.

It rejects the same invalid inputs (rdf:nil, lists of length <2, unrecognized nodes) and raises TypeError for Literals.
Edge-case comparison with the reference (run on scratch copy): ordinary invalid inputs match in exception class; only the message text differs, and messages are not part of the contract.

Divergence: the candidate tests `is not None` (shacl.py:65, 70, 83, 87, 91) where the reference uses walrus truthiness (reference shacl.py:59, 63, 77, 81, 85). For an empty-string IRI as the value of sh:inversePath or a modifier, the candidate returns InvPath(URIRef("")) / MulPath(URIRef(""), ...), while the reference raises SHACLPathError. The reference behaviour there is incidental, not specified, and no test covers it, so I am not counting this as a failure.
Neither the reference tests nor the candidate tests cover this divergence.
